To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ectopic expression in a cell-type-specific context can be exploited to silence a specific gene as an approach to regulate gene-expression in human diseases.
ectopic expression and activity of a transcription factor in a cell-specific-context can be used to regulate gene expression as a therapeutic approach.
ectopic expression in a cell-specific-context of transcription factors can be used to target and silence the expression of specific genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of ectopic expression of transcription factors to silence the expression genes of interest.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of human disease, particularly retinal diseases, and the development of gene therapy vectors for use in these applications.
the identification of novel therapeutic targets and strategies to treat inherited and age-related retinal degenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that ectopic expression (in the context of a cell-specific promoter) of a TF can silence the expression of the gene of interest in vivo.
the ectopic expression of Krüppel like factor-15 can be used to selectively silence a gene of interest.
the authors have shown that ectopic expression can be used to regulate gene expression as a therapeutic approach in human disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ectopic expression of TFs in a cell-specific-context can be used to target specific genes in a therapeutic manner.
we can use ectopic expression of TFs in a cell-specific manner to target and silence a specific gene in a cell-type specific manner.
we show that ectopically expressed KLF15 can be targeted to a specific DNA sequence present in the promoter of rhodopsins and can silence the expression of rhodopsinin rod photoreceptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ectopic expression of an otherwise ubiquitous transcription factor can be used to specifically silence the expression of an endogenous gene.
ectopic expression can be a useful tool for silencing genes.

ectopic expression (in this case, in the context of the rod photoreceptor) of a transcription factor (KLF15, in this case) that has a putative DNA binding site in the promoter region of a gene (RHO, in this case), can be used to regulate the expression of that gene in a cell-specific manner, with limited genome-wide perturbation.
